It is commonly expressed in mass of oxygen consumed over volume of solution which in SI units is milligrams per litre (mg / L).

In the titration method for determining COD, the excess dichromate is reacted with a reducing agent, ferrous ammonium sulphate. As the ferrous ammonium sulphate (FAS) is added slowly, the excess dichromate is converted into its trivalent form.

questions.solution:
According to Graham’s Law, at constant pressure and temperature, molecules or atoms with lower molecular mass will effuse faster than the higher molecular mass molecules or atoms. Thomas even found out the rate at which they escape through diffusion. In other words, it states that rate of effusion of gas is inversely proportional to the square root of its molecular mass. This formula is generally used while comparing the rates of two different gases at equal pressures and temperatures. Formula can be written as

Rate1Rate2=M2M1

M1 is the molar mass of gas 1

M2 is the molar mass of gas 2

Rate1 is the rate of effusion of the first gas

Rate2 is the rate of effusion for the second gas

It states that rate of diffusion or effusion is inversely proportional to its molecular mass.

questions.q: The figure represents PV vs P relation for CO,CH4,H2 and He gases under identical conditions. Which curve, shown in the figure, represents He gas?
questions.solution:
To understand the deviations from ideal behaviour, let us first see how the real gases show deviations from Boyle’s law. According to Boyle’s law, PV = constant, at constant temperature. Hence, at constant temperature, plot of PV vs. P has to be a straight line which is parallel to x-axis. However, the real gases do not show such a behaviour as shown in figure no. 1 Below.

From the plots, we observe that for gases like H2 and He, PV increases continuously with increase of pressure whereas for gases like CO, CH4 etc. PV first decreases with increase of pressure and reaches a minimum value and then increases continuously with increase of pressure. Similarly, if we plot experimental values of pressure versus volume at constant temperature (that is, for real gas) and theoretically calculated values from Boyle’s law (that is, for ideal gas) the two curves do not coincide as shown in figure no. 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is false during adsorption of gas molecule on a metal surface?
options: Both enthalpy and entropy simultaneously decreases
questions.solution:
According to the question, Adsorption is reversible in nature and is dependent on pressure as well as temperature. An increase in pressure decreases the volume of gas and thus increases the adsorption of gas molecules. Conversely, a decrease in pressure will cause the removal of gas molecules from the solid surface.

The amount of heat evolved when one mole of an adsorbate (gas or liquid) is adsorbed on the surface of an adsorbent is called enthalpy of adsorption. The enthalpy of adsorption for chemo sorption is larger than that for physical adsorption. The magnitude of enthalpy of adsorption for chemo sorption & physical adsorption are  in order of -400 Kj per mol and -20 to -40 Kj per mol.

questions.solution:
Given the system of equations 2x+9y+5z=8, 2x+3y-z=-4 and x-2z=-5 have an infinite number of solutions given byx=-5+at, y=2+bt, z=ct, t∈R then x, y, z will satisfy the given equations.

Thus, we have 2-5+at+92+bt+5ct=8, 2-5+at+32+bt-ct=-4 and -5+at-2ct=-5

⇒-10+2at+18+9bt+5ct=8, -10+2at+6+3bt-ct=-4 and -5+at-2ct=-5

⇒2at+9bt+5ct=0, 2at+3bt-ct=0 and at-2ct=0

⇒2a+9b+5c=0, 2a+3b-c=0 and a-2c=0.

From the third equation, we get a=2c, put this value in any of the first two equations, to get

2×2c+9b+5c=0

⇒b=-c.

Thus, we have a:b:c=2c:-c:c

⇒a:b:c=2:-1:1.

Hence, the solution can be a=2, b=-1, c=1.

questions.solution:
Three integers are selected at random from 3n consecutive integers.

G2:x+1, x+4, x+7...... ,x+3n-2

G3: x+2, x+5, x+8,.....x+3n-1

So, the sum of three randomly selected integers from the given set of integers must be divisible by 3,

Either all are being selected from the same group or 1 integer from each group.

Possible ways of selecting three integers from the same group=C3n+C3n+C3n=3·C3n=3×n!3!×n-3!=nn-1n-22

Possible ways of selecting one integers from each three mentioned groups

=C1n×C1n×C1n=C1n3=n3

So, The number of favourable ways=nE=n3+nn-1n-22=2n3+nn2-3n+22=3n3-3n2+2n2

And the number of sample space=C33n=3n!3!3n-3!=3n×3n-13n-26

So, the probability=nEnS=3n2-3n+23n-13n-2.
